name: live_sum_over_no_matching_rows_is_null
description: SUM over an empty set returns NULL rather than zero; the analyzer marks it nullable and this fixture makes a live engine demonstrate the NULL instead of assuming it
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE users (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now())
CREATE TABLE orders (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), total NUMERIC(10, 2) NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now())
query_sql:
-- @name GetOrderTotalSum
-- @returns :many
SELECT SUM(total) AS total_sum FROM orders ORDER BY total_sum

columns.name: total_sum
columns.note: SUM returns NULL over an empty set even though total is NOT NULL

sqlc_comparison.sqlc_behavior: sqlc marks SUM(total) non-nullable because total is NOT NULL in the schema, which is wrong for an empty set
sqlc_comparison.scythe_improvement: scythe marks any bare aggregate nullable, and the first run here has no orders at all, so the engine actually returns the NULL rather than the fixture asserting it in the abstract

default: INSERT INTO users (id, name, email) VALUES (1, 'Ada Lovelace', 'ada@example.com')
INSERT INTO orders (id, user_id, total) VALUES (1, 1, 42.50)
